svg.aria-label: Architecture map of Strobe Assistant showing where the Cognito ID token travels, the three places it is verified, and which calls use IAM roles instead
svg.title: Strobe Assistant (A2) — where the token travels and where it is checked
svg.text: Strobe Assistant (A2) — where the token travels and where it is checked
One Cognito ID token goes browser → agent → MCP server → A1 API and is verified by every service it reaches (V1–V3). Inside AWS, services reach models and data
with their own IAM roles — the user's token never unlocks AWS, it only decides whose data is asked for.
signs in through the A1 login API
keeps the ID token in sessionStorage
never sends it in a URL
logs in as an enrolled account
no user token at all — IAM role only
reads userId from the S3 key
one agent instance per WebSocket connection

text.tspan: for the life of the connection
→ re-checks exp; expired = sign in again
browser can't choose where tools live
model never sees the token or a userId

svg.text: the only component with data access

text.tspan: injected server-side, not in any tool schema
token to the A1 API (checked again by V1)

svg.text: authorised by each task's IAM role — no user token involved
presigned GET for the caller's own image · 300 s
forward the same Bearer token, so A1's own
authorisation rules apply — no second, weaker
A1 routes, including MCP's get_post calls
managed by AWS: pool JWKS, iss, aud, exp
exp re-checked on each session/new and prompt
makes the MCP server safe on its own
AWS API call signed with an IAM role (SigV4) — no user token
